info.summary: OpenAPI-first contract for Amplitude CLI, MCP, SDK, and docs.
info.description:
Public developer-facing API contract for Amplitude resources.
This spec is intended to be the canonical source for generated CLI, MCP tools,
SDKs, and documentation.

get.description:
Returns saved cost, efficiency, and quality findings, ranked by magnitude
times confidence. These are periodically evaluated findings, not live
queries. Healthy and closed findings can remain visible. Thumbs-downed
findings are excluded. Use each finding's project_id for individual reads.

parameters.name: agent_name
parameters.description: Exact agent name. Omit for all scopes; an empty string selects project-level findings only.

200.description: Saved findings and an opaque next-page cursor. Keep the same project and agent filter when paging.

get.summary: Get a saved Agent Analytics insight
get.description: Returns one finding by its stable UUID and own project_id. Missing, cross-project, and thumbs-downed findings return 404.

parameters.name: insight_id
parameters.description: Stable insight UUID returned by the list operation, not a finding key such as tool-failures.

post.description:
Creates an empty dataset. Add sessions with the dataset sessions endpoint.
`name` is not an identity key, so repeating a create makes another dataset,
even with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

Listing and reading datasets is served by the Agent Analytics MCP read
surface, not by this API.

agent_name.description: Scope the dataset to one agent. Omit for a project-level dataset.

patch.description:
Updates dataset metadata. Absent fields are unchanged; an explicit `null`
clears `description`. `id`, `agent_name`, and `source_type` are immutable —
create a new dataset to change the agent scope.

post.summary: Add sessions to an Agent Analytics dataset

200.description: Dataset after the sessions were added, with refreshed counts.

delete.summary: Remove sessions from an Agent Analytics dataset
delete.description:
Removes sessions from a dataset. The sessions themselves are untouched;
only their dataset membership is removed. Sessions that are not in the
dataset are ignored, so the call is safe to repeat.

Takes the same body as the add operation, so an add is undone in one call
rather than one call per session. `dry_run=true` validates the dataset and
the session ids without mutating, returning `204` on a hit and `404` if the
dataset does not exist.

204.description: Sessions removed from the dataset, or dry-run hit.

post.description:
Creates an evaluator in the inactive state. Activation is a separate
permission and is not exposed by this API — activate in the Agent Analytics
UI once the evaluator has been reviewed.

`tags` constrains what a result may record. Supplying them for a `binary` or
`categorical` evaluator is what keeps results to a known set of values
rather than free-form model output.

Listing and reading evaluators is served by the Agent Analytics MCP read
surface, not by this API.

tags.description: Required for `binary` and `categorical` evaluators.

patch.description:
Updates an evaluator addressed by its stable identifier. Absent fields are
unchanged. Each update creates a new inactive version; the response `id` is
that new version, and `stable_id` is unchanged.

Updating does not activate. An evaluator already active in the UI keeps
serving its current active version until the new one is promoted there.

tags.description: Replaces the full tag set when present.

get.description:
Returns eval runs for the project, most recent first. A run is a batch
evaluation of sessions by one or more evaluators; it is asynchronous, so a
freshly triggered run is returned with a pending status and no results.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter to runs in one lifecycle state.

200.description: Eval runs and an opaque next-page cursor.

post.summary: Trigger an Agent Analytics eval run
post.description:
Starts an asynchronous eval run and returns it immediately with a pending
status. Poll the run by id, or read results through the Agent Analytics read
surface once it completes.

Target the run either at a dataset or at a session list, not both. Caps are
enforced server-side: 10 evaluators and 100 targeted sessions per run.
For larger datasets, only the first 100 members are targeted and the
acceptance response includes a truncation warning. This selection warning
is not persisted on the run returned by later get/list calls.

evaluator_ids.description: Evaluator version identifiers returned by create or update. Evaluator updates use stable identifiers instead.

dataset_id.description: Evaluate the sessions in this dataset. Mutually exclusive with `session_ids`; exactly one of the two is required.

session_ids.description: Evaluate these sessions. Mutually exclusive with `dataset_id`; exactly one of the two is required.

sample_size.description:
Retained for compatibility. This endpoint targets explicit session
IDs, including when expanding a dataset, so sample_size does not
reduce the selected sessions. All supplied IDs are targeted,
with dataset expansion capped at the first 100 members.

get.summary: Get an Agent Analytics eval run
get.description:
Returns one eval run by id, including progress counters and, once the run
finishes, cost and latency. Per-session results are read through the Agent
Analytics read surface, not here.

Returns the MCP servers configured for the project. A project with no MCP
servers returns 200 and an empty `data` array.

200.description: MCP servers for the project. The list is complete, so `has_more` is false.

get.description:
Returns the server's active topic tree. The resource id is the server id.
A visible server with no pinned taxonomy returns 200, null run fields, and
`nodes: []`. An unknown server returns 404.

parameters.name: server_id
parameters.description: Server id.

parameters.name: parent_id
parameters.description:
Node selector. Omit it for every node in the active tree. `root`
returns root nodes. Any other value is a stable topic id and returns
that topic's direct children. An unknown parent returns 404 when a
taxonomy is pinned.

get.description:
Returns one topic and up to eight example episodes. Examples are not a
page. Use the episode list to page through episodes.

parameters.name: server_id
parameters.description: Server id.

parameters.name: topic_id
parameters.description: Stable topic id. `root` is not a topic id.

get.description:
Returns a page of episode summaries for one topic. The default page size
is 25 and the maximum is 100. Keep the same filters
when following `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: server_id
parameters.description: Server id.

parameters.name: topic_id
parameters.description: Stable topic id.

parameters.name: started_after
parameters.description: Include episodes that started at or after this RFC 3339 timestamp.

parameters.name: started_before
parameters.description: Include episodes that started before this RFC 3339 timestamp.

parameters.name: lane

parameters.name: client_name

parameters.name: auth_type
parameters.description: Exact stored auth type.

parameters.name: has_error

parameters.name: is_thrash

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from `pagination.next_cursor` on the previous response.

parameters.name: limit

200.description: Episode page. Keep the same filters when requesting the next cursor.

get.description:
Returns one episode, including its project, server, auth type, and topic
breadcrumb. A missing or cross-project episode returns 404.

parameters.name: episode_id
parameters.description: Episode id returned by the topic or episode list.

get.summary: List tool calls in an MCP episode
get.description:
Returns the complete episode tool flow in event time and event id order, including recorded
properties, rationale, duration, and errors. Properties are returned as
recorded; individual input or output fields may be absent.
A missing or cross-project episode returns 404.

parameters.name: episode_id
parameters.description: Episode id returned by the topic or episode list.

200.description: Complete ordered tool call list. An existing episode with no recorded calls returns an empty list.

post.description: RFC 8628 device authorization endpoint. Initiates the device flow and returns a device_code, user_code, and verification URIs for the user to approve out of band, then poll the token endpoint. When `offline_access` is requested, `openid` is also required.

post.summary: Sign up for an Amplitude account
post.description: Sign up for an Amplitude account. The response either provides credentials for the new account or starts an OAuth flow to complete signup.

200.description: Signup result with credentials, an OAuth flow, or additional signup information.

500.description: Signup could not be completed due to a server error.

503.description: Signup authentication service is temporarily unavailable.

post.description: RFC 6749 §3.2 token endpoint. Supports the `device_code` grant (RFC 8628) and the `refresh_token` grant. Authenticated by the fixed confidential device-flow client (injected server-side). Does not require a Bearer token.

400.description: Invalid or unsupported grant (RFC 6749 §5.2 OAuth error).

Returns projects visible to the authenticated principal.

Provides the API key for a project. A project ID is required when the
organization has more than one project.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: The project ID. Required when the organization has more than one project.

200.description: The project API key alongside the project name and ID.

If the endpoint is temporarily unavailable, retry later.

post.summary: Check recent event ingestion with an ingestion API key
post.description:
Checks whether Amplitude received any events for the project associated
with the supplied ingestion API key during the preceding eight hours.

`observed` means at least one event was received in the evaluated window.
`not_observed` means no events were received. `inconclusive` means no events
were found, but the available data could not confirm their absence. Use the
returned window when reporting or comparing results.

The window uses server upload time: when Amplitude received each event,
rather than the event time supplied by the sender.

Provide `polling_timeout_seconds` to request server polling guidance.
While another check is advised, successful responses include
`poll_after_seconds`; its omission means clients should stop polling.

api_key.description: Ingestion API key for the Amplitude project to check.

200.description: Recent event ingestion status for the evaluated window.

status.description:
`observed` when at least one event was received;
`not_observed` when none were received; `inconclusive`
when none were found but their absence could not be
confirmed.

basis.description:
The window is based on when Amplitude received each
event.

401.description: The supplied API key is invalid.

example.title: Invalid API key
example.detail: The supplied API key is invalid.

502.description:
The ingestion status could not be determined. Retryable responses use
`unreliable_dataset_response` or `upstream_error` as the `error_code`.

get.description: Returns the skills currently available for implementing Amplitude, with each skill's name and when-to-use description.

name.description: Identifier used to retrieve the skill.

get.description: Returns the requested skill document verbatim as markdown, including frontmatter.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Skill identifier as listed by `GET /v1/skills`.

200.description: The requested skill document as markdown.

post.description:
Checks whether events reached an Amplitude project during a recent time
window. Provide `event_type` to check one exact event type, or omit it to
check for any event. The default lookback is 10 minutes. The returned
window can begin up to five minutes earlier so the evaluation covers the
complete starting interval.

`observed` means at least one matching event was found. `not_observed`
means no matching event was found in the evaluated window. `inconclusive`
means no matching event was found, but complete recent data was not
available to confirm its absence. Use the returned window when reporting
or comparing results.

This POST computes a result and does not mutate state, so it does not
require an `Idempotency-Key`.

Provide `polling_timeout_seconds` to request server polling guidance.
While another check is advised, successful responses include
`poll_after_seconds`; its omission means clients should stop polling.

value.title: Endpoint unavailable
value.detail: This endpoint is unavailable for your organization.

502.description:
The ingestion status could not be determined. Retryable responses use
`event_type_not_queryable`, `unreliable_dataset_response`, or
`upstream_error` as the `error_code`.

get.summary: List event properties for an event
get.description:
Returns properties bound to a specific event, including ingested-only
properties (those with `is_in_schema: false`). Use the `is_in_schema`
flag to detect whether a `PATCH` will succeed before issuing it.

post.description:
Creates an event property and adds it to the project's tracking plan
(`is_in_schema: true` after success). If the property already exists in
the schema, the existing resource is returned without modification.
If the property exists ingested-only (`is_in_schema: false`), this call
promotes it into the schema with the metadata supplied here.

patch.description:
Updates metadata on an event property. Returns `422 not_in_schema` if
the property is ingested-only (`is_in_schema: false`); promote it via
`POST` first. Field absent means leave unchanged; field with `null`
clears (where allowed). `enum_values` and `classifications` replace the
array entirely — there is no per-item add/remove.

422.description:
Property is not part of the project's tracking plan. Returned when
attempting to PATCH a property with `is_in_schema: false`.

get.summary: Export a tracking plan as CSV
get.description:
Streams a CSV export of the project tracking plan, in the same format as
the Events and User Properties downloads in Data. Exports the default
branch unless `branch_id` or `branch_name` selects another one, and
includes that branch's unpublished changes.

When `type=events`, optional `event_names` filters rows to exactly matching
event names (case-sensitive). Matching event rows and their event-property rows
plus referenced property-group definition rows are returned, preserving the CSV
format and headers expected by import.
`event_names` is not accepted with `type=user_properties`.

Unknown names are returned in `X-Unmatched-Event-Names` as URL-encoded,
comma-separated names. Set `strict=true` to fail with 422 instead when any
requested event name is unknown. Deleted events count as unknown when
`include_deleted=false`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Export format. Defaults to `events`.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.description: Optional branch identifier. Mutually exclusive with `branch_name`.

parameters.name: branch_name
parameters.description: Optional branch name. Mutually exclusive with `branch_id`.

parameters.name: include_deleted
parameters.description: Include deleted events or properties in the export.

parameters.name: lookback_days
parameters.description: Lookback window in days for the volume and query columns of the `events` export. Defaults to 30. Ignored for `user_properties`.

parameters.name: event_names
parameters.description:
Optional event-name filter for `type=events`. Repeat this parameter
(`event_names=a&event_names=b`) and/or pass comma-separated values
(`event_names=a,b`). GET comma-separated values trim surrounding
whitespace from each split segment. Matches are otherwise exact and
case-sensitive.

parameters.name: strict
parameters.description:
When true, return 422 if any requested `event_names` are unknown.
When false (default), unknown names are reported in
`X-Unmatched-Event-Names`.

X-Unmatched-Event-Names.description: URL-encoded, comma-separated unknown event names from `event_names` (present only when `strict=false` and unknown names exist).

X-Unmatched-Event-Count.description: Total number of unknown event names, including names omitted from the header when truncated.

X-Unmatched-Event-Names-Truncated.description: True when `X-Unmatched-Event-Names` was truncated to stay within header size limits.

504.description: The export did not start in time.

post.summary: Export a tracking plan as CSV (JSON body variant)
post.description:
Exports tracking-plan CSV with the same response semantics as `GET` export.
Use this variant when `event_names` is long and would exceed URL limits.
Request `Content-Type` must be `application/json`.

branch_name.description: Optional branch name. Omit for default branch.

branch_id.description: Optional branch identifier. Mutually exclusive with `branch_name`.

lookback_days.description: Lookback window in days for `events` volume/query columns. Ignored for `user_properties`.

event_names.description: Optional event-name filter for `type=events`. Matches are exact and case-sensitive. Not accepted with `type=user_properties`.

strict.description: When true, return 422 if any requested `event_names` are unknown.

X-Unmatched-Event-Names.description: URL-encoded, comma-separated unknown event names from `event_names` (present only when `strict=false` and unknown names exist).

X-Unmatched-Event-Count.description: Total number of unknown event names, including names omitted from the header when truncated.

X-Unmatched-Event-Names-Truncated.description: True when `X-Unmatched-Event-Names` was truncated to stay within header size limits.

504.description: The export did not start in time.

post.summary: Import a tracking plan from CSV
post.description:
Sends a tracking-plan CSV as the request body and applies it to a new import branch.
This endpoint always imports into a branch and never writes to main directly.
Creating the branch publishes any pending changes on main's staging version
first, as creating a branch in the product does. When the import fails after
the branch was created (422 for invalid rows, 502 for a server failure), the
error payload includes `details.branch` so callers can inspect or delete the
branch. A duplicate `branch_name` returns 409 before anything is created.

parameters.name: branch_name
parameters.description:
Optional name for the import branch, 1 to 256 characters. When omitted,
the import uses `import`, or `import-N` if that name is taken. A name
that already exists returns 409.

requestBody.description: The CSV file contents, at most 50 MB.

201.description: Import completed on an import branch.

import_type.description:
Public import target type. `events` includes event, template,
event-property, and template-property rows; `user_properties`
includes user-property rows.

breakdown.description:
Per-type import counters. Units:
- templates/events/user_properties: definition rows changed.
- template_properties/event_properties `created|updated`:
  property definition rows changed.
- template_properties/event_properties `unmapped`: properties
  removed from templates/events; the property definition is kept.

409.description:
The requested `branch_name` already exists. Nothing was created; choose
another name.

422.description:
The CSV is not valid tracking-plan data. `details.branch` is present when
the error was found after the import branch was created.

502.description:
The import did not finish. Not retryable when `details.branch` is present
(the branch was created) or when the connection was lost mid-import (the
import may have started): a retry could create a second branch. List the
project's branches to find the result. A 502 without `details.branch`
that is marked retryable means the import was never started.

504.description:
The import did not respond in time and may still complete. Not
retryable: a retry may create a second branch. List the project's
branches to find the result.

get.summary: List scheduled event deletions and blocks

200.description: Successful response. Defaults to pending actions.

post.description:
Each `event_type` must already exist on the project and may appear only once
in `items`. Update and cancel take scheduled-action ids, so they do not look
up the event again.
One pending scheduled action is allowed per event type. If that event
already has a pending deletion or block, cancel it before creating another.
The whole request fails if any item cannot be created.

delete.description: The whole request fails if any id is not a pending scheduled action on the project.

List user properties for a project

post.description:
Creates a user property and adds it to the project's tracking plan.
Same idempotency semantics as creating an event property.

patch.description:
Updates metadata on a user property. Returns `422 not_in_schema` if the
property is ingested-only. Same patch semantics as updating an event property
(field absent = unchanged, `null` = clear, arrays replace).

Only `display_name`, `description`, `is_hidden`, and `classifications`
are mutable via PATCH today. Type/shape fields (`data_type`,

`is_official` is read-only in this API version.

Property is not part of the project's tracking plan. Returned when

get.description:
Returns saved charts in the project. Results are paginated with cursor-based
pagination. Chart definitions are omitted; use GET chart with
`include_definition=true` to retrieve a read-only definition.

Pagination uses an opaque numeric cursor (offset into the current sorted
search result set). Each list query can access at most **10,000** matching
charts from the search index; pages beyond that window return fewer items
and `next_cursor: null` even when more charts may exist in the project.
Use filters (`q`, `chart_type`) to narrow large projects.

Sortable fields are `updated_at` and `name`; prefix with `-` for descending.
Defaults to `-updated_at` (most recently updated first). `created_at` is not
supported in this API version.

Returns chart metadata. The chart definition is omitted by default. Set
`include_definition=true` to include a read-only definition object. The
definition shape is unstable and not intended for authoring.

post.description:
Computes and returns normalized results for a saved chart. v1 supports
`event_segmentation`, `sessions`, `funnels`, and `retention` chart types;
other chart types return `422` with `error_code: unsupported_chart_type`.
Results reflect the authenticated caller's project access and chart
permissions.

This POST computes a result and does not mutate state. It is therefore a
read operation and does not require an `Idempotency-Key`.

Omitting `time_range` uses the chart's saved range; if the chart has no
saved range, the server defaults to the last 30 days.

Query is synchronous with bounded defaults. Expensive queries may return
`504` when exceeding the server timeout; async query jobs are planned for
a follow-up slice. Retryable responses may include retry advice where
their endpoint-specific error contract provides it.

422.description:
Chart type is not supported for public query in this version. The
request was understood but cannot be processed. Returned with
`error_code: unsupported_chart_type`; `detail` names the chart type
and the currently supported set.

get.description:

put.description:
Replaces the customer-managed AI context for a project in
Settings → AI Controls. Send `"context": ""` to clear the stored value.
Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header on every request.

get.description:
Returns saved metrics in the project. Results are paginated with cursor-based
pagination. Full metric definitions are included in list responses.

Sortable fields are `updated_at` and `name`; prefix with `-` for descending.
Defaults to `-updated_at` (most recently updated first).

Returns the full saved metric definition including type-specific params,
version, and metadata.

post.description:
Returns click counts for one page URL, grouped by the CSS selector of the
clicked element or by page coordinate, ranked by count. Filter by device
viewport band and date range. Results reflect the authenticated caller's
project access and data access controls.

This POST computes a result and does not mutate state. It is therefore a
read operation and does not require an `Idempotency-Key`.

Omitting `time_range` uses the last 30 days in the project timezone. The
span of `time_range` cannot exceed 90 days.

Returns the scroll-depth distribution for one page URL as a cumulative
histogram from the top of the page, plus the average fold and the deepest
scroll observed. Filter by device viewport band and date range. Results
reflect the authenticated caller's project access and data access
controls.

This POST computes a result and does not mutate state. It is therefore a
read operation and does not require an `Idempotency-Key`.

Omitting `time_range` uses the last 30 days in the project timezone. The
span of `time_range` cannot exceed 90 days.

Returns one metric for every zone on a page URL, ranked by value. A zone
is identified by the CSS selector of its element. Results reflect the
authenticated caller's project access and data access controls.

This POST computes a result and does not mutate state. It is therefore a

Omitting `time_range` uses the last 30 days in the project timezone. The

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Filter this list by an exact flag key within the project. Returns the standard list response, or an empty list when no active flag matches. Get, update, and archive require the returned numeric id; those operations do not accept a flag key or resolve one automatically.

key.description: Lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores only.

patch.description: Updates feature flag metadata and rollout settings. Variant, tester, deployment, and link mutations will be exposed through dedicated subresources in a later slice.

get.description:
Returns guides in the project. Results use the standard
Developer API list envelope with cursor pagination (`cursor`, `limit`).

Full-text search (`q`) and custom sort orders are not supported yet.

parameters.name: created_by
parameters.description: Filter by creator email or login id (exact match).

post.description:
Creates an unpublished draft guide. Publish, schedule, and test
instrumentation are not available via API in v1. At most one content
variant is accepted on create; the `control` key is reserved.

parameters.name: include_unpublished_changes
parameters.description:
When true, return the latest draft (unpublished edits) when one exists.
Default false returns the live published guide.

parameters.name: include_translations
parameters.description:
When true, add `localization` (the project's default locale and other
locales) and each variant's `translations` and `translation_status`.
Read with `include_unpublished_changes=true` before writing
translations, so keys and `latest_version` match the draft. When
localization is disabled in the project settings, only
`localization: {enabled: false}` is added.

patch.description:
Updates metadata, targeting, and content variants. For published guides,
changes apply to a draft until publish in the UI. `latest_version` is
required and must match the current draft, otherwise the update returns
`409`. The check runs before the write rather than atomically with it, so it
reduces but does not fully prevent lost updates from concurrent writers.

available via API in v1. Status fields on the response are derived read-only.
When `variants` is sent, it must list every existing variant by `id` with

pagination (`cursor`, `limit`). List items omit `config`; get a theme

Creates a guides and surveys theme. Both the live theme and the draft
start as Amplitude's built-in default theme, and `config` is merged into
the draft (see `ThemeConfigPatch`), so you only send the values you want
to change. Nothing changes for users until the draft is published in
Amplitude. The response carries the draft `config`.

The new theme isn't the default unless the platform has no default theme
and you can publish theme changes, in which case Amplitude makes it the
default, as it does in the theme editor. A `platform` that isn't enabled
for the project returns `400`. Publishing, archiving, and changing the
default theme are not available via API.

Returns a guides and surveys theme. `config` is the live theme by default.

Renames a theme or changes its draft. `config` is merged into the current
draft (see `ThemeConfigPatch`): send only the values you want to change,
and `null` to reset a value to Amplitude's built-in default. The live theme
is not changed; publish the draft in Amplitude. The response carries the
full draft `config`.

To make sure nobody changed the theme since you read it, send the
`updated_at` from your last read; if the theme has changed since, the
update returns `409` and nothing is written. Omit `updated_at` to skip the
check: concurrent patches then both apply, and a later one wins for any
value both set. The check runs before the write rather than atomically
with it, so it narrows but does not close that window. Internal themes
return `409` with
`error_code: theme_is_internal`; edit them on their guide or survey in
Amplitude.

server-side in an ephemeral cache; you receive the public key (paste into
your Snowflake user via `ALTER USER <user> SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY = '...'`) and
an ephemeral ID to pass as `snowflake_private_key_ephemeral_id` in the
destination `config` on a subsequent `POST /destinations` for a Snowflake
direct-load destination.

This is the CLI equivalent of the "Generate RSA Key" step in the Amplitude
UI wizard, so customers do not have to run `openssl genrsa` and manage
private keys locally.

Server id. It stays stable when a new run is pinned and is present when nothing is pinned.

examples.description: At most eight episode summaries. This is not a page and has no cursor.

id.description: Stable topic id, ordered from the root.

properties.description: Recorded event properties. Contents depend on the instrumented tool; input and output fields may be absent.

grant_type.description: The OAuth grant type. Must be `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`.

device_code.description: The device_code from the device-authorization response.

grant_type.description: The OAuth grant type. Must be `refresh_token`.

refresh_token.description: The refresh_token issued by a previous token or refresh grant.

RecentEventIngestionPollingTimeoutSecond.description:
Maximum polling window requested by the caller. Clients should complete
the initial check even if it exceeds this window and use the window only
to limit subsequent polls. Its presence requests polling guidance; it is
not an HTTP request timeout, and each HTTP request performs one check.

RecentEventIngestionPollAfterSeconds.description:
Minimum seconds to wait before the next ingestion check. Returned only
when polling was requested and another check is advised. Its omission
means the server does not advise another check.

ResultKind.description:
High-level shape of the normalized result payload. Adapters set this
explicitly per supported chart type; `unknown` means the server could not
classify the result shape safely.

RecommendedAggregate.description:
Recommended aggregation method for downstream consumers. Non-additive metrics
(e.g. unique users) must not be summed across intervals. `unknown` is used
when the adapter cannot determine a safe aggregate; treat values as
non-additive in that case.

additive.description:
When false, values must not be summed across time intervals or groups
without understanding deduplication semantics.

role.description: Role of this dimension in the result.

x.description: Dimension value (typically an ISO date or category label).

complete.description:
When false, the interval is incomplete (current bucket). Only present
when `exclude_incomplete_datapoints` is false.

aggregate.description: Optional pre-computed aggregate for the series.

AnalyticsResultData.description:
Normalized result payload. Populated fields depend on `result_kind`.
Timeseries and funnel results use `dimensions` and `series`. Table results
use `columns` and `rows`.

AnalyticsResultMetadata.description: Echo of effective query parameters and chart context.

group_by_limit.description: Applied group-by limit when breakdown was truncated.

time_series_limit.description: Applied time-series limit when buckets were truncated.

context.description: Customer-managed markdown or plain text; empty when unset.

Full customer-managed context to store. Replaces the existing value;
send an empty string to clear.

PropertyType.description: Property namespace for filters, group-bys, and aggregations.

group_type.description: Group type for group properties. Empty string for non-group.
Group type for group properties. Empty string for non-group.

group_by.description:
Properties to group by. Required for formula metrics that use property
aggregation functions like `PROPSUM(A)` or `PROPAVG(A)`.

count_group.description: What to count. `User` for unique users, `Event` for event totals.

events.description: Event definitions referenced by letter (A, B, C...) in the formula string.

formula.description:
Formula string. Reference events by letter. Functions include
`UNIQUES(A)`, `TOTALS(A)`, `PROPSUM(A)`, `PROPAVG(A)`, `PROPMIN(A)`,
`PROPMAX(A)`, `PROPCOUNT(A)`, `PROPCOUNTAVG(A)`, `REVENUETOTAL(A)`.

return_on.description: Number of intervals to return on.

return_on_interval.description: Interval length in days. `1` for daily, `7` for weekly, `30` for monthly.

FunnelPathsToCollect.description:
Whether the funnel measures unique users completing the path or total
conversion path counts.

conversion_seconds.description:
Maximum time window to complete the funnel, in seconds
(e.g. `86400` = 1 day, `604800` = 7 days).

funnel_constant_properties.description: Properties held constant across funnel steps.

MetricDefinitionUnknown.description:
Placeholder definition for metric types this API version does not model.
No type-specific fields are returned.

PageUrl.description:
Page URL to analyze. Accepts `http` and `https` URLs; a URL without a
scheme is treated as `https`. The query string and fragment are removed
before matching, so `https://example.com/pricing?utm=x` and
`https://example.com/pricing` are the same page.

HeatmapUrlMatch.description:
How `page_url` is matched against the page URL recorded on each event.
`is` matches the exact URL, `contains` matches any URL containing it,
`has_prefix` matches URLs starting with it, and `glob` treats `*` as a
wildcard.

HeatmapDeviceType.description:
Viewport band to include, matching the device selector in the product:
`desktop` is at least 1440 px wide, `laptop` is 900 to 1440 px, `tablet`
is 500 to 900 px, `mobile` is at most 500 px. Use `custom` with
`viewport_width` to match one exact width.

ViewportWidth.description:
Exact viewport width in pixels. Required when `device_type` is `custom`
and not accepted otherwise.

selector.description: CSS selector of the clicked element.

count.description: Clicks (`metric: totals`) or unique users (`metric: uniques`).
Clicks (`metric: totals`) or unique users (`metric: uniques`).

depth_from_px.description: Lower bound of the scroll-depth bucket in page pixels.

depth_to_px.description: Upper bound of the scroll-depth bucket in page pixels.

sessions_reached.description: Sessions that scrolled at least to this bucket.

percent_reached.description:
`sessions_reached` divided by the sessions counted in the first
bucket, as a fraction. The first bucket is always `1`.

ZoningUrlMatch.description:
How `page_url` is matched against the page URL recorded on each event.
`is` matches the exact URL; `contains` matches any URL containing it.

ZoneMetric.description:
Metric computed per zone. Rates are fractions (`0.18` is 18%).

- `click_rate_pageview`: page views with a click in the zone, divided by page views.
- `click_rate_session`: sessions with a click in the zone, divided by sessions.
- `rage_click_rate_pageview`: page views with a rage click in the zone, divided by page views.
- `rage_click_rate_session`: sessions with a rage click in the zone, divided by sessions.
- `click_distribution`: clicks in the zone, divided by all clicks on the page.
- `click_recurrence`: clicks in the zone, divided by page views. Can exceed 1.
- `rage_click_recurrence`: rage clicks in the zone, divided by page views. Can exceed 1.
- `exposure_rate`: page views where the zone was visible, divided by page views.
- `attractiveness_rate`: page views where the zone was visible and clicked, divided by page views where it was visible. Can exceed 1.
- `revenue_per_click`: revenue attributed to the zone, divided by sessions that clicked it, in the project's revenue unit.

value.description: The metric value for this zone. Rates are fractions and are returned uncapped.

RolloutWeights.description: Variant-keyed rollout weights. Values may be normalized to sum to 100 (percentages) or expressed as unnormalized relative weights (for example `{ "control": 1, "treatment": 1 }` for an even split). Weights are non-negative and may be fractional.

prop.description: Property name or cohort identifier being targeted.

prop_type.description: Namespace of the targeted property, for example `user`, `event`, or `group`. Omitted for conditions that target a cohort rather than a property.

op.description: Targeting operator applied to the property values.

values.description: At least one value to match against. Conditions with no values are rejected.
User IDs, device IDs, or cohort identifiers included in this variant. At most 2000 entries per variant (the limit is 10 when the entries are cohort identifiers).

deployments.description: Deployment IDs associated with this flag. Managed via the create/update deployment fields, not set directly on this field.

bucketing_key.description: Bucketing key used for assignment. Never null in responses; defaults to `amplitude_id` when not explicitly set.

version.description: Server-managed config version used for optimistic concurrency.

archived.description: Whether the resource is archived. Set via the archive (DELETE) operation.

NudgePlatform.description:
Target platform. Guides and surveys without an explicit platform are
returned as `web`.

NudgeType.description: Whether the resource is a guide or a survey.

NudgeStatus.description: Derived rollout state. Read-only on API responses.

url.description: Page URL or pattern for the URL match types.

isExclude.description: When true, matching pages are excluded.

operator.description: How this rule combines with the next one.

value.description:
CSS selector of an element that must be on the page. Required for
`domSelector`, which is web only.

GuideSurveyPageTarget.description:
One page rule. An empty list means every page. Keys stay camelCase, and
no other keys are allowed. Send `url: ""` with `domSelector`.

object.description: Resource discriminator. `guide` or `survey` on the public API.

key.description:
Feature flag key that controls delivery. Matches the
`[Guides-Surveys] Key` property on SDK-tracked guide and survey events,
so use it to join events to this guide or survey.

start_at.description: Scheduled start of the live flag. `null` when no start is scheduled.

end_at.description: Scheduled end of the live flag. `null` when no end is scheduled.

url.description: Admin URL for the guide or survey.

page_target_segments.description: Pages where the guide or survey is eligible. Empty means every page.

latest_version.description:
Monotonic version for optimistic concurrency. Send the value from the
latest GET on PATCH; a stale value returns 409.

GuideSurveyVariantKey.description:
Variant key within the nudge: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`.
Keys must be unique. `off` is reserved, and `control` can't be given to
a new variant.

GuideSurveyModalPosition.description: Where a modal or popover sits in the viewport.

GuideSurveyStepLayout.description: Arrangement of media and text in the step.

sticky.description: Keep the banner on screen while the page scrolls.

anchor.description: CSS selector the pin attaches to.

isShowingMask.description: Dim the rest of the page.

advanceTrigger.description: CSS selector whose click advances to the next step.

skipIfNotFound.description: Skip the step when the anchor is missing.

GuideSurveyTooltipMarker.description:
The marker users hover or click to open the tooltip. Every marker type
also accepts `width` (number) and `elementIsMarker` (boolean).

anchor.description: CSS selector the tooltip attaches to.
CSS selector the card attaches to.

GuideSurveyStepFormFactor.description:
Step layout. `type` selects it. Every form factor also accepts
`zIndexOverride` (number or null) and `textAnimation` (`typewriter`).
Modal, popover, pin, tooltip, and card accept the step layout keys
`layout`, `mediaPosition`, `contentAlignment`, `titleAlignment`, and
`footerLayout`; banner and checklist accept a narrower set. Tooltips and cards can't be snoozed.

value.description: Markdown text. Inline HTML is allowed and is sanitized on save.

action.description: Optional link opened when the image is clicked. No other action type is allowed.

src.description: Video URL, for example a YouTube, Vimeo or Loom link.

type.description:
Common actions:
- `step_forward`, `step_back`: go to the next or previous step.
- `complete`: finish the guide or survey.
- `dismiss`: close it.
- `snooze`: hide it for a while, with optional `interval` (`hour`, `day`, `week`) and `value`.
- `go_to_step`: jump to a step. `value` is the 0-based position of the step in the variant's `steps`, not its id.
- `link`: open the URL in `value`; `operation` is `self` (same tab), `blank` (new tab) or `router`.
- `nudge`: start another guide or survey. `value` is its numeric id, and `productType` is `guide` or `survey`.
- `no_action`: no action of its own. The button still advances: to the next step, or on the last step it finishes the guide or survey. The dashboard's survey templates use it for the submit button. It does not keep the user on the step; `stay_on_step` does.

Buttons built in the dashboard can also use `stay_on_step`,
`click` (`value` is a CSS selector), `callback`, `app_review`,
`open_resource_center`, `open_ai_assistant`, `open_chat`, `document`,
`video`, and `use_conditional_logic`. Send those back unchanged.

grow.description: Stretch the button to fill the footer row.

actions.description:
Optional action sequence the dashboard writes for buttons with side
effects: `{type: "action_sequence", navigation: <action>, effects: [<action>]}`.
When present, the SDK runs it instead of `action`, so update both or
neither.

message.description: Error shown when a required question is left empty. Required when `value` is `true`.

type.description: `survey_text` is a multi-line answer; `survey_text_short` is a single line.

prompt.description: Placeholder shown in the empty answer field. Required; send `""` for none.

userProperty.description: User property whose value fills the answer.

GuideSurveyTextQuestionBlock.description: Free-text survey question. Put the question itself in a `markdown` block or the step `title`.

options.description:
Number of choices on the scale. Allowed values depend on `type`:
`stars` 3 or 5, `numbers` 3, 5, 7 or 10, `emojis` 2, 3 or 5, and
`nps` 10.

emojis.description: Exactly one emoji per option. Required when `type` is `emojis`.

property.description: Property of the event that triggered the survey.

GuideSurveyHiddenFieldBlock.description: Not shown to the user. Adds a value to each survey response.

GuideSurveyContentBlock.description: One content block. `type` selects the block and the shape of `meta`.

GuideSurveyStepContent.description:
The step body: content blocks rendered top to bottom, below the step
`title`. `meta` keys are camelCase. Keep a block's existing `uuid` when
you edit it, because survey responses are keyed by it; a block sent
without one (or with `null`) is given one on save. To change one block,
send the step's whole `content` array back with that block edited. Send
`[]` for an empty step, not `null`.

A step can have at most one `markdown` block, one `image` or one `video`
(not both), two buttons, ten survey questions, and ten `survey_hidden`
fields. Survey question blocks are only allowed in surveys, and only on
steps with the `classic` or `vertical` layout. A checklist item can have
at most one button. A snooze button needs the variant's `snooze_label`.

meta.value: Track any event in two clicks.

id.description: Container id, unique within the step.

GuideSurveyContentV2Container.description:
A block-builder container. `children` are containers or content blocks,
plus the `title` and `step_counter` blocks that only exist in trees.

GuideSurveyTitleBlock.description: The step title inside a block-builder tree.

GuideSurveyStepCounterBlock.description: Shows the step number inside a block-builder tree.

GuideSurveyStepContentV2.description:
Block-builder layout: a tree of `layout` containers whose `children`
are containers or content blocks, including the step's `title` block.
Returned only on steps built in the block builder; when present, the
dashboard and SDK render this tree, not `title` and `content`.

On update, only accepted on resources that already have a step with a
tree; a flat-only guide or survey can't be converted through the API.
On create, any step may take one, so a resource read with `content_v2`
can be copied. Block `uuid`s must be unique within the step. Keep a block's
existing `uuid` when you edit it, because survey responses are keyed by
it; a block sent without one is given one on save. The saved tree is
normalized to the shape the block builder saves, and the step title is
taken from its `title` block. On a step with a tree, send `title` and
`content` only together with `content_v2`. Not supported on banner or
checklist steps or on mobile platforms. `null` switches the step back
to `content`.

GuideSurveyStepInput.description:
Step payload on create/update. `id` is optional — omit for new steps; include
when updating an existing step row. A negative `id` is a step added to a
published guide or survey's draft that has not been published yet.

title.description: Step title. Omit it to leave it unchanged; `null` is rejected.

sort_key.description: Ignored on input. Steps are shown in the order of `steps`.

GuideSurveyVariantInput.description:
Variant payload on create/update. `id` is optional — omit for new variants;
include when updating an existing variant row. A negative `id` is a variant
added to a published guide or survey's draft that has not been published yet.
`variant` key is required. Create doesn't take translations: create the
guide or survey, then send `translations` with an update.

display_title.description: Variant title. Omit it to leave it unchanged; `null` is rejected.

snooze_label.description: Snooze button label for this variant. Omit it to leave it unchanged; `null` is rejected.

done_label.description: Label of the last step's button. Omit it to leave it unchanged; `null` is rejected.

GuideSurveyImmediateTrigger.description:
`immediately` shows as soon as the page matches. `none` does not fire on
its own. Neither accepts `data.delay`, and neither can be combined with
other triggers.

subprop_op.description: Comparison operator, for example `is`, `is not`, or `contains`.

delay.description: Milliseconds to wait after the trigger fires. Omit it rather than sending null.

sessionPropertyFilters.description:
Session property conditions. The inner arrays are AND groups, and
the outer array ORs them.

GuideSurveyBehaviorTrigger.description: Fires on user behavior. `user_confusion` and `exit_intent` are web only.

delay.description: Milliseconds to wait after the element appears or is clicked.

GuideSurveyElementTrigger.description: Fires when a CSS selector appears or is clicked.

event.description: Analytics event type that fires the trigger.

event_count.description: Times the event must occur. Omitted means once.

delay.description: Milliseconds to wait after the event count is reached.

filters.description: Event property conditions. Every condition must match.

value.description: How long to wait on the page before showing.

GuideSurveyAfterTimeTrigger.description:
Fires after the user has been on the page for `value` `unit`s. Does not
accept `data.delay`.

GuideSurveyTrigger.description: One trigger. `type` selects which fields `data` uses.

GuideSurveyTriggerConfig.description:
When the guide or survey appears. One trigger, or an array of triggers
where any match fires it. Nested keys keep their stored names (`selector`,
`event`, `event_count`, `delay`, `filters`). Don't send `null`: the dashboard can't open a
guide or survey without a trigger. Send `{"type": "immediately"}` to
show right away.

periodCount.description: How many `period`s the limit covers. Omitted means 1.

GuideSurveyLifecycle.description:
How often the guide or survey may show again. `periodCount` is camelCase;
the other keys are snake_case. Send the whole object, not `null`.

value.description: Stop after this many survey responses. Required when `enabled` is true.

recurrence_period_days.description: Days over which impressions are spread evenly. Always required when `even_distribution` is sent.

GuideSurveyTranslationValue.description:
Translated text. `content.survey_list` keys take an array of option
labels in the same order as the source; every other key takes a string.
Markdown and title HTML is sanitized like step content.

GuideSurveyTranslations.description:
Stored translations, locale to translation key to text. Returned with
`include_translations=true` and on updates that send translations.

GuideSurveyTranslationStatus.description:
What is left to translate. `sources` lists every translatable key with its
current default-locale text. Per locale, `missing` keys have no
translation and `outdated` keys were translated from text that has since
changed.

payload.description: Optional JSON payload associated with the experiment variant.

GuideSurveyLocalization.description:
The project's localization settings. `locales` are the languages other
than `default_locale` that translations can be written for. Configure them
in project settings. When localization is disabled, only `enabled: false`
is returned and variants carry no `translations` or `translation_status`.

temporarily_hide_page_target_segments.description: Page rules that are saved but not currently applied.

theme_id.description:
Theme applied to this guide or survey. `null` means the project's
default theme for the platform. Fetch it with the Themes API.

experiment_variants.description: Read-only experiment variant keys when the nudge is experiment-backed.

flag_config.description:
The Experiment feature flag that delivers this nudge, in the same
shape as the Feature Flags API. Includes audience targeting
(`target_segments`) and rollout. With
`include_unpublished_changes=true`, draft rollout and targeting
settings are applied over the live flag.

GuideSurveyTranslationsInput.description:
Locale (one of `localization.locales`) to translation key to text.
Merged into the stored translations: keys you leave out are kept, `null`
clears a key, and `null` for a locale clears every key in it.

Keys name a field by where it sits in the variant: `display_title`,
`display_description`, `snooze_label`, `done_label`;
`steps[<step id>].title`; and block fields as
`steps[<step id>].blocks[<block uuid>].<field>`, for example
`content.markdown`, `content.title`, `content.button[primary]`,
`content.survey_rating.lowerLabel`, or `content.survey_list`. Copy keys
from `translation_status.sources` instead of building them. A key must
name a field that has default-locale text.

GuideSurveyVariantUpdateInput.description:
Variant payload on update. `id` names an existing variant. `variant` may be
omitted; when sent it must equal the stored key. An entry that carries only
`id` and `translations` is translation-only: a list made of
translation-only entries may name a subset of the variants. Any other
field on any entry makes it a content update, which must list every
variant.

display_title.description: Variant title. Omit it to leave it unchanged; `null` is rejected.

snooze_label.description: Snooze button label for this variant. Omit it to leave it unchanged; `null` is rejected.

done_label.description: Label of the last step's button. Omit it to leave it unchanged; `null` is rejected.

ThemeVariablesPatch.description:
Variables to set, or `null` to reset a variable to its default. Setting a
name that isn't a known theme variable returns `400`. `null` is
accepted for any name, so you can remove one stored earlier.

ThemeVariables.description:
CSS variable values keyed by variable name. Colors accept any CSS color
(`#ff0000`, `rgb()`, `color-mix()`, `var(--token)`). Sizes need a unit
(`12px`, `1.5rem`, `100%`). Numbers such as font weights may be JSON
numbers or numeric strings. Any value may reference another variable with
`var(--name)`.

DestinationConnectorKind.description:
Authoritative connector kind on a destination. `event`/`identify`/`cohort`
are for streaming and cohort destinations; `warehouse_export` is for
warehouse-export destinations. Routing is derived from the array of these
values, so there is no separate routing field. `warehouse_export` cannot
be combined with the other kinds.
